solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Choice digging tool

definitions.meaning: your ... is your choice or selection
a pointed tool for breaking ground

explanation.surface: Someone recommending the best implement for working the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a pick is both the selection one makes and a pointed implement for breaking hard earth.

clue.text: Documents quietly placed on copiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
apers are those who ape, that is copy, others

explanation.surface: Office papers being laid gently on the photocopying machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers are official documents, such as identity papers or a collection of files.

clue.text: Chef having bottom pinched: that's a surprise

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, and pinched means stolen, so it is taken off

parts.note: a cook is a chef

explanation.surface: A cook is groped in the kitchen and someone exclaims in shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is a British exclamation of surprise or wonder, much like 'gosh'.

clue.text: Ring salesman perhaps, to scoff, around spring

indicators.note: around says the scoffing word wraps round the spring word

parts.note: to jeer is to scoff or mock
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A man selling rings is mocked as he stands near a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller sells rings among other gems and ornaments; 'perhaps' marks rings as one example of his wares.

clue.text: Barges Les manoeuvred around front of ship

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the ship's front
manoeuvred means moved about, so the letters of Les are rearranged

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A man called Les steers canal barges around a ship's prow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barges' looks like a noun for boats, but it is a verb: to barge is to shove. 'manoeuvred' makes ELS, and 'around' puts BOW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow one's way is to push roughly through people, which is what someone who barges does.

clue.text: Foolish person's face might have this urge

definitions.text: Foolish person's face might have this
definitions.meaning: someone shown up as foolish is said to have ... their face

explanation.surface: A remark about a fool's embarrassed expression, then a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'egg on one's face' means embarrassment, while the phrasal verb 'egg on' means to spur somebody into action.

clue.text: Letters to acquire at cricket ground

parts.note: to land something, such as a job, is to acquire it
Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: Alphabet characters to be picked up at a sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' pretends to be letters of the alphabet; here it means people who let property. LORD'S is the London home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords rent out property, so they are literally those who let rooms or houses to tenants.

clue.text: Rex needs a break — most unusual

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A man named Rex needs time off because something very odd has happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common, so most unusual.

clue.text: For safety's sake, a motorist should be quiet!

definitions.text: For safety's sake, a motorist should
definitions.meaning: a motorist should fasten the seat belt

explanation.surface: Road safety advice that ends with a sharp command for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Belting up means fastening a seatbelt, and as British slang it is a rude command to stop talking.

clue.text: Wise words show real brains, primarily

parts.note: to prove is to show something to be true

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each of the two following words is taken

explanation.surface: Sage sayings demonstrate genuine intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying expressing a general truth or piece of advice.

clue.text: Go close, ignoring a person beyond hope?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ignoring says the following letter is left out of the word for close

parts.note: near means close

explanation.surface: An instruction to approach without attending to someone who is past saving.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or past saving, informally; the question mark admits the loose fit.

clue.text: Deny King Edward, for example, has returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: King Edward is a variety of potato, which is a tuber

explanation.surface: A monarch rejecting something on his return to the realm.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a well-known British potato variety, not the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to deny it or argue that it is false.

clue.text: Fights to obtain what's missing for air rad precautions

indicators.note: to obtain means to hold or get, so the word for fights contains the missing thing

parts.note: bouts are fights, as in boxing
a lack is what is missing

explanation.surface: Boxing bouts held to secure supplies lacking during air raids.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'air rad', a slip for 'air raid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackouts were wartime measures in which all lights were hidden so enemy bombers could not see targets.

clue.text: Kilns we built specially for seafood

indicators.note: built specially means constructed in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ovens have been custom-made for cooking shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Winkles are small edible sea snails, a traditional British shellfish snack.

clue.text: Record to have when going across mountains

indicators.note: going across says the word for when spans the record, holding it inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Taking an album along while travelling over a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the great mountain range of central Europe.

clue.text: A grate leaving a small gap?

parts.note: to grate is to jar, that is to irritate or rasp

explanation.surface: A fire grate that does not fit, leaving a little space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like the fireplace noun, but it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open, with a small gap between it and the frame.

clue.text: Catchy tune from Jack by the fireplace

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A man called Jack hums a song while sitting by the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A jingle is a short memorable tune, especially one used in advertising.

clue.text: Imposing jiujitsu — guards to mount displays

indicators.note: to mount says the hidden letters are read backwards
displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A martial arts fighter's defence on show while climbing aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'to mount' means going upwards, so the letters 'displays' reveals are read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means dignified and awe-inspiring, which is what something imposing is.

clue.text: Cheers up, on course to get fit

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this piece comes first
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
a tack is a sailing course, a direction taken

explanation.surface: Raising a toast while on a racecourse to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like the adjective for healthy, but it is a noun: a fit of coughing is an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit and an attack are both sudden bouts of illness or emotion.

clue.text: Bishop with skill, fine composer

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
art is skill, as in the art of conversation
OK means fine

explanation.surface: A bishop who is talented at music, a fine composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Dishevelled drunk emptying pockets

indicators.note: pockets is a verb here: the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A messy drinker turning out their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' looks like a noun being emptied, but it is the verb meaning holds inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt means untidy in appearance, especially hair or clothing, as dishevelled does.

clue.text: Among bananas, a different fruit

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mixed in among the bananas is another kind of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' poses as the fruit, but is slang for mad. The definition is 'a different fruit': one other than bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit, other than the banana mentioned in the surface.

clue.text: Girl's cosy home, close to Chelsea

definitions.note: read as 'Girl is': the 's links the name to its wordplay

parts.note: a nest is a cosy home

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A young woman's snug flat sits near the Chelsea area of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a female first name, of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Shelled nuts beside vase making quite a change

indicators.note: shelled means the outer casing is removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: Peeled nuts set down next to a vase transform the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete reversal of direction or policy, so a dramatic change.

clue.text: No fewer than twelve ultimately entering after all

indicators.note: entering says that letter goes inside the phrase for after all

parts.note: at last means after all, finally

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A dozen arrivals, give or take, finally coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: At least means a minimum of, so not less than the stated amount.

clue.text: Old boxer appearing in tabloid regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A retired fighter features often in a popular newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was a heavyweight boxing champion, now dead, so 'old' fits.

clue.text: Finally got us hose for clumps of grass

indicators.note: finally means the last, so the end letter of the word is taken

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

explanation.surface: At last someone bought a garden hose for watering grassy tufts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests the garden kind; here it is hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussocks are dense tufts or clumps of coarse grass.

clue.text: Ed's escaped from evil, incendiary band

indicators.note: escaped from means got out of, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: wicked means evil
Ed's is read as 'Ed has': the name gives its own letters

explanation.surface: A man named Ed has fled a wicked gang of arsonists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' poses as a group of people; here it is a strip of material.
explanation.definitionFit: A wick is a strip of fibre in a candle or lamp that carries fuel to the flame and burns.
